response.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination x WHERE x.ID = p.ID AND x.`ANA Pattern` = 'S') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL), AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The condition is applied per patient. Any patient with at least one examination whose ANA Pattern is 'S' is excluded entirely. The average then covers all of the remaining patients' examinations, including those with a NULL pattern. Only patients with at least one examination appear.
The average is the plain AVG, which ignores NULLs and is not rounded. Patients whose aCL IgM values are all NULL have a NULL average and sort last.

alternatives.interpretation: The condition is applied per examination row. Examinations with pattern 'S' are dropped and the average is taken over the remaining examinations. Patients with other, non-S examinations are kept. Rows with a NULL pattern are kept.
alternatives.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_aCL_IgM FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE COALESCE(e.`ANA Pattern`, '') <> 'S' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY (AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) IS NULL), AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) DESC LIMIT 10
